10.1002_aenm.71167: Dendrite growth and interfacial instability fundamentally limit the reversibility of aqueous zinc metal batteries. Artificial solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) are typically constrained by an intrinsic trade‐off between mechanical rigidity for dendrite suppression and flexibility to accommodate volume fluctuations. Here, inspired by the sliding filament mechanism of biological muscle, we construct a mechanically adaptive ultrathin interphase that reconciles rigidity with deformability through dynamic hydrogen‐bond‐mediated stress dissipation. A nanoscale reinforced architecture, composed of rigid graphene oxide (GO) backbones interconnected by Triton‐induced sacrificial hydrogen bonds, enables controlled interlayer sliding while preserving structural integrity. The resulting ∼80 nm interphase simultaneously delivers a high Young's modulus (22.4 GPa) and tensile strain (∼12%), effectively overcoming the modulus–flexibility constraint. Meanwhile, the interphase promotes Zn 2+ desolvation and stabilizes the interfacial microenvironment. Consequently, Zn||Cu cells deliver over 10000 cycles at 5 mA cm −2 with an average coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.93% and a cumulative capacity exceeding 10 Ah cm −2 . Zn||MnO 2 cells operated at a low N/P ratio of 2.5 exhibit markedly improved cycling stability. This work establishes a mechanically adaptive interphase design principle for stabilizing zinc metal anodes.
10.1002_anie.8162603: Precise regulation of the coordination environment in iron‐based single‐site catalysts (Fe SSCs) is essential for promoting the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) toward efficient hydrogen peroxide production. However, the atomic‐scale relationship between coordination structure and reaction pathway remains insufficiently understood. In this work, a series of iron molecular catalysts with tunable axial coordination were rationally designed to systematically investigate how ligand‐mediated regulation of the metal site and ligand conjugation direct the 2e − ORR pathway. Combined electrochemical measurements, in situ spectroscopic analysis, and theoretical calculations demonstrate that electron‐rich Fe centers weaken *OOH adsorption, thereby enhancing H 2 O 2 selectivity. In contrast, increased ligand conjugation modifies the local catalytic microenvironment, strengthens oxygen intermediate adsorption, and reduces H 2 O 2 selectivity. A linear structure‐activity relationship between the Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ redox potential and H 2 O 2 selectivity is established, identifying this redox potential as a reliable descriptor for rapid catalyst screening. When the optimal Fe‐NHC/Py(−H) catalyst was integrated onto monolayer graphene to form a gas diffusion electrode, it delivered 97.6% Faradaic efficiency and an H 2 O 2 yield of 72.9 mol g cat −1 h −1 at 400 mA cm −2 . These findings provide mechanistic insights for designing highly selective 2e − ORR electrocatalysts via coordination engineering.
10.1016_j.jece.2026.124279: This study investigated the early-stage aggregation of polystyrene latex (PSL) particles under turbulent flow generated by orbital shaking in a U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) baffled flask, for which the turbulent flow and the energy dissipation rate ( ε ) of turbulence were well-characterized. The turbulent aggregation rate coefficients of PSL particles above the critical coagulation concentration showed good overall agreement with the Brunk–Koch model without fitting parameters using the reported value of ε and a widely accepted value of the Hamaker constant. This agreement indicates that orbital shaking in an EPA baffled flask provides an experimentally accessible platform for quantifying turbulence-induced aggregation of microplastic colloids and for relating mixing intensity to aggregation kinetics under controlled conditions. The resulting framework may support future investigations of particle aggregation under environmentally relevant ionic strengths and in more complex microplastic systems relevant to natural and engineered waters.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c07791: High-performance dielectric capacitors with exceptional energy storage capabilities are indispensable for the development and implementation of state-of-the-art electronic and electric power systems. Nonetheless, synchronously attaining dual-high recoverable energy storage density (Wrec) and efficiency (η), as well as satisfactory thermal stability, remains a formidable challenge, restricting the practical applications of capacitive devices toward miniaturization and low-energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate high energy storage in core–shell-structured relaxor ferroelectrics by constructing heterogeneous polymorphic structures to decouple the mutual constraints between critical energy storage parameters. By designing polymorphic heterostructures featuring distinct differences in polar fluctuations and distributed nanoclusters, alongside disordered oxygen octahedral tilts and intensified lattice distortions, we effectively suppress hysteresis, polarization saturation, and remnant polarization under high electric fields while achieving enhanced breakdown field strength (Eb) and high maximum polarization. Phase-field simulations further substantiate the substantial enhancement in Eb in this distinctive heterogeneity. Leveraging this structural design, we simultaneously realize a high Wrec of 8.32 J/cm3 and a high η of 85%, as well as excellent broad-temperature stability (Wrec > 3.95 J/cm3 at 200 °C), outperforming most relaxor dielectrics. This study offers a feasible and effective paradigm to guide the exploitation of high-performance relaxors for advanced high-efficiency capacitors.
10.1038_s41467-026-78830-0: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO43−) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO43− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint. A solar-powered electrocoagulation system rapidly removes low-level phosphate from natural waters via interfacial ion concentration, overcoming mass-transfer limits for efficient decentralized water purification with low energy and material use.
